evidence.method: families transplant (template main:080b1a14 / select_party_member.c, score 8129bp) seeded an m2c control-flow recovery over the complete symbolized owner, cross-checked callee signatures against already-exact siblings (battle/effects/objects/spawn_linked_resource_object.c, battle/effects/burst_particles/run_main_object.c, battle/effects/object_control/resume_object.c, battle/effects/heavy_impact/finish.c, and three Func_08092054 sites)

notes: This is a battle-effect spawn routine: it looks up the caller's object (Func_08092054(arg0)) and a fixed shared object (Func_08092054(Data_02000240[125])) to derive a palette/style word, plays three sound-and-window beats (Func_08096bec/Func_08092560/Func_08009158 x3), classifies a kind value read through the object's field+0x50/+0x28 into one of three timing constants, then spawns and links a fixed 8-entry chain of child objects via Func_080090c8 before a closing beat and Func_08091750() return. No loop over player input at all -- the family match is purely on instruction-shape/register-pressure cosine similarity, not semantics. Every non-trivial callee signature here (Func_08092054(s32), Func_080090c8 4-arg, Func_08009080/Func_080091e0/Func_08009240 2-arg, Func_080925cc(id,1)) is independently confirmed by five already-adopted exact siblings, so the call shape and argument counts are solid, including catching that the raw m2c draft's two 'unset register' Func_08092054 reads are actually genuine calls with the function's own r0 argument (a single s32 parameter) reused verbatim rather than zero-arg calls.

The raw m2c draft (0 params, garbage self-referential `sp0 = &sp0 + 0x10` for the 8-entry object array, narrow types) scored badly on a first read; declaring the real `s32 Func_0809537c(s32 arg0)` signature, replacing the array-address garbage with an explicit `void *list[8]; void **list_ptr = list;` (matching the field's own persisted-pointer idiom seen on 08029554 and 08021488), and fixing the two Func_08092054 call sites to pass `arg0` and `Data_02000240[125]` respectively brought the candidate to 560 vs 564 bytes, 118 wrong instructions on the first scored attempt -- within 4 bytes of exact.

Remaining disagreement is narrow: (1) the shared 'style' value that survives from the two Func_08092054 lookups through all three beat calls sits in `fp` in the reference but `r9` in every candidate tried (a register-allocation swap of the same kind seen on every other owner in this batch); (2) a small negative bitmask (`field &= -0xD`) compiles to a single `movs r3,#0xF3` immediate load in the candidate but to a two-instruction `movs r3,#13; negs r3,r3` materialization in the reference -- tried both an outer-cast and an inner-cast spelling of the same expression with no change, so this is a genuine instruction-selection choice tied to some other part of the expression context, not the cast placement.

This reads as a last-mile compiler-scheduling/selection residual on an otherwise fully confirmed call sequence and field layout, not a remaining source-shape gap -- the closest of the four measured-drafts in this batch (4 bytes short) and a good candidate for permuter-style bounded search.
No external source, copied instruction bytes, inline assembly, fixed-register variable, compiler barrier, or compiler modification was used.
